David Haig’s thoughtful, engaging drama has two 1920s pop-culture titans grapple with themes of faith, fraud and self-deception

Images - Manuel Harlan In the 1920s, Sir Arthur Conan Doyle was as famous as it gets really, author of the beloved Sherlock Holmes stories, a polymath and a rare British example of that most continental of figures, the public intellectual.
Wanting to believe in something that brings you great comfort, whether it’s true or not, is very desirable in our turbulent world.
